newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The central government should consider decentralising certain police functions and devolving some political authority to the policing ministers in the provinces, according to a task team appointed by national policing minister Sydney Mufamadi.

- Several government ministers and their departments have agreed on a pilot project with major implications for future senior public service appointments. It includes performance agreements detailing key responsibilities, delivery targets and evaluation criteria.
- The benchmark R150 government long bond pierced the 14 percent yield level on Friday amid expectations of bullish economic indicators which would justify an interest rate cut.

- JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo met representatives of the European Commission last week to discuss the mining group's purchase of Anglo American Corp 26.8 percent stake in Lonrho. The parties remained silent on the outcome, but analysts believed EC approval for the deal was imminent.
- Tweefontein mine management had begun dismissing large numbers of workers it believed were involved in killing a manager at the colliery's Waterpan section last week, a mine spokesman said.
- Gentyre shareholders have opted to restructure the company into holding company Forward Corp, despite a call by the Shareholders' Association of South Africa to reject the plan.

- The African National Congress has demanded an unreserved apology from the Nigerian government after remarks by Foreign Minister Walter Ofonagoro that South Africa was a white country with a black head of state.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Barbrook, a small gold mine outside Barberton in Mpumalanga province has closed down. The mine, owned by Caledonia Mining, fell victim to the crisis in the gold industry.
- Economists remained cautious about an early cut in the bank rate by the Reserve Bank, despite a surge of positive economic indicators expected to hit the financial markets this week.
- JCI has sold its entire 8.7 percent holding in Johnson Matthey, the world's leading platinum group metals marketer.
- Beacon Sweets and Chocolates is offering a 10,000 rand reward for information leading to the arrest of the killers of two temporary workers brought in during a strike which is continuing.
SAKE-BEELD

- The Australian economy would carry the burden of the fall in the gold price after the announcement that the country's central bank sold 167 tonnes of gold, says Robert Pringle, head of the public policy centre of the World Gold Council.
- The South African Reserve Bank's latest syndicated borrowing facility of $1.75 billion is about $250 million more than the original amount planned.
- Senwes, formerly the SentraalWes agricultural marketing cooperative which was transformed into a company in April, hopes to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange within a year or so.
